items.q: For routine urine analysis, the sample the book recommends is:
opts: The 2nd urine sample of the morning, by midstream technique
A random sample taken after vigorous exercise
Urine collected from the urobag of a catheterised patient
items.exp: The line reads: Sample — 2nd urine sample of morning → midstream technique. The first morning void is not what is printed, and catheterised patients must give fresh urine, never urobag urine. (Book p740)

items.q: Fill up: Urine must be analysed within ______ hours at room temperature, while the pH should be checked immediately.
items.exp: Analysis: within 2-4 hours at room temperature (pH to be checked immediately). (Book p740)

items.q: Up to how long may a urine sample be stored at 2-8°C before analysis?
The preservatives listed for a urine sample are:
A marathon runner is scheduled for a routine urine check. To avoid false results from rhabdomyolysis, strenuous physical activity must be avoided for how long before collection?
items.exp: Strenuous physical activity 72 hrs prior to collection → false results due to rhabdomyolysis. (Book p740)

items.q: Which statement about urine collection is TRUE?
opts: Collection during menstruation should be avoided
Urine may be collected from the urobag in catheterised patients
Strenuous exercise just before collection improves sample quality
pH can reliably be checked after a day at room temperature
items.exp: To avoid: strenuous activity 72 hrs prior and collection during menstruation; pH is checked immediately. (Book p740)

items.q: Fill up: In catheterised patients, urine must always be collected ______ and never from the urobag.
items.exp: Catheterised patients: always collect fresh urine; do not collect from urobag. (Book p740)
